summary: This House resolution honors by name the 363 law enforcement officers killed in the line of duty during 2025 and expresses congressional support for police, recognition of their sacrifices and need for resources, and condolences to their families.

scores.thoughts: The resolution contains no provisions, authorizations, or references related to federal, state, or local government expenditures, appropriations, or budgets. It is purely a symbolic memorial resolution.
The bill makes no mention of taxes, tax policy, rates, deductions, or revenue measures of any kind.
No references to healthcare systems, coverage, providers, or policy appear in the text.

While the resolution honors officers killed in the line of duty (many of whom die from gunfire), it does not propose, reference, or take any position on gun regulations, background checks, ownership rights, or related legislation.
The resolution has no content related to immigration, border policy, visas, asylum, or enforcement of immigration laws.
No provisions or language concerning reproductive rights, abortion access, or related regulations are present.
The bill addresses only civilian law enforcement officers and contains nothing about military forces, defense budgets, or national security spending.
No environmental, climate, regulatory, or conservation provisions are included.
The resolution does not address welfare programs, food assistance, unemployment benefits, or any social safety-net policies.
No references to schools, education funding, curriculum, or school choice appear.
The bill contains no language on drug enforcement, decriminalization, sentencing for drug offenses, or related policies.

The resolution explicitly expresses 'unwavering support for law enforcement officers' and recognizes the need for them to receive 'equipment, training, and resources' to protect the public. This constitutes a clear, albeit symbolic and non-legislative, statement of support for policing and law enforcement, aligning with the +1 end of the spectrum (tougher sentencing and policing) rather than reform or rehabilitation-focused approaches. The effect is minor because the measure is purely commemorative.
No provisions or references to trade agreements, tariffs, globalization, or protectionism are present.
The resolution does not discuss deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No content related to LGBTQ+ legal protections, rights, or policies appears.
The bill addresses only domestic law enforcement and contains nothing about foreign aid or international assistance.
No references to voting access, election integrity, voter ID, or electoral reform are included.
The resolution has no provisions concerning technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance policy.
No language addresses unions, collective bargaining, worker protections, or employer flexibility.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination policy.
